title: Be honest.
paragraphs: Be honest.

Not the version of you that shows up on Sundays.
Not the version that posts verses when life is going well.
The real you.

Do you actually love God…
or do you just love what He gives you?
Because there’s a difference. And you’ve felt it.

You’ve prayed hard when things were falling apart.
You’ve cried out when you needed help.
You’ve made promises in moments of desperation.

“God, if You just fix this… I’ll follow You.”
“God, if You get me through this… I’ll change.”
And for a while, you meant it.

But then the crisis passed.
The pressure lifted.
The blessings came.

And slowly… quietly…
your pursuit of Him faded.

God didn’t move.
You did.

You didn’t stop believing in Him.
You just stopped needing Him.

God saw it.
You knew.

There’s a kind of relationship with God that is built entirely on benefits.
Provision. Protection. Peace. Favor.
And when those things are present, you feel “close” to Him.
But remove the benefits… and everything changes.
That’s the test no one wants to talk about.

Because Scripture doesn’t ask, “Do you enjoy God’s blessings?”
It asks something far deeper.
“Do you love Him?”
Jesus didn’t soften this.
“If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.” — Luke 14:26
Read that again.

He wasn’t calling for emotional hatred.
He was exposing priority.

Do you love Him above everything…
or just alongside what He gives?
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You can follow God for years and still be centered on yourself.

You can worship and still be using Him.
You can serve and still be negotiating with Him.
You can obey… but only when it benefits you.
That’s not love.
That’s a transaction.
And God doesn’t enter into transactions for your soul.
He goes after surrender.
There was a moment when Jesus turned to a crowd—people who had just been fed miraculously—and said something that shattered their expectations:
“You are seeking Me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate your fill of the loaves.” — John 6:26
He exposed them.

They didn’t want Him.
They wanted what He could do for them.
And when He stopped feeding them… they left.
That same pattern is still alive today.

You don’t notice it when life is easy.
You don’t question it when prayers are answered.

But the moment God feels silent…
the moment things don’t go your way…
the moment obedience costs you something—
That’s when the truth surfaces.
Do you still follow Him then?
Or do you drift?
Be honest.
Because Job stood in that exact place.

Everything stripped away.
Wealth gone.
Children gone.
Health broken.
And his wife said what many people think but don’t say:
“Curse God and die.” — Job 2:9
In other words—He’s not worth it anymore.
No more benefits. No more reason to stay.
But Job answered with something that cuts straight through shallow faith:
“Though He slay me, I will hope in Him.” — Job 13:15
That’s love.

Not because God gives.
But because God is.
That’s the kind of relationship God is calling you into.

Not convenience.
Not conditional loyalty.
Not spiritual bargaining.
Love.
Real love.
The kind that says—

Even if the blessings stop…
Even if the healing doesn’t come…
Even if the breakthrough never happens…
He is still worthy.
Because the Gospel was never about temporary benefits.
It was about something far deeper.

You weren’t just struggling.
You were dead in sin.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
Not slightly off. Not mostly good.
Fallen.
Separated.
And no amount of “blessings” could fix that.
So God didn’t just give you help.
He gave you Himself.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
That’s the turning point.

Not when your life improves…
but when your heart is confronted.
Jesus didn’t go to the cross to upgrade your circumstances.
He went to rescue your soul.

To pay for your sin.
To restore what you broke.
To reconcile you back to God.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” — Ephesians 2:8
A gift.

Not earned.
Not negotiated.
Not deserved.
So ask yourself again—

Do you love God…
or just what He gives you?
Because one of those will walk away when it gets hard.
And the other will cling to Him… even when everything else is gone.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
There’s a depth most people never reach because they never move past surface-level faith. Not inspiration. Transformation.

Say it plainly.
“I want to love God, not just His blessings.”
Type it. Own it.
Someone you know is living off borrowed faith and silent compromises—send this to them. Not to judge them, but because you see where it leads.
You’ll need to read it again when your motives start shifting.
